subject: Lumen4b: intermittent 504s — temporary fallbacks, throttles, and next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lucy Chang <lucy@brightretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Lumen4b: intermittent 504s — temporary fallbacks, throttles, and next steps

Hi Lucy —

Quick update from our side: starting ~07:40 PDT we observed a spike of 504 / timeout responses for Lumen4b serving your production traffic. Impact estimate so far is ~6% of requests to the Lumen4b endpoint for Bright Retail (higher for longer prompt lengths).

What we’ve done immediately:
- Enabled a client-facing graceful-fallback to the Lumen4b-compact-quant variant for requests that exceed 3s server processing time.
- Applied a conservative token-level throttle and smoothed admission control to reduce amplification from retries.
- Turned on enhanced request tracing and increased log retention for the affected models.

Short-term ask for you:
- Please add a 2s client-side timeout with exponential backoff (100ms -> 500ms -> 1s) for non-critical calls where you can tolerate a retry.
- If you can, route high-latency prompt types to the /v1/variants/lumen4b-compact endpoint while we stabilize.

We will share a metrics dump and the runbook we used to triage. Expected next update in ~3 hours or earlier if we have a full mitigation. Deep apologies for the disruption — we know this is critical during your promotional window and we’ll prioritize Bright Retail on the recovery.

Attachments: [lumen4b-throttle-metrics-100K.csv], [incident-runbook-lumen4b.pdf]

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Lumen4b: intermittent 504s — temporary fallbacks, throttles, and next steps

Karthik / team —

Thanks for the heads-up. Notes from triage so far (ops):
- Root cause signal points to a regression in one of the attention kernels that sporadically amplifies compute for certain long-context meshes. Reproducer attached in the diagnostics folder.
- We’ve pushed a hot patch to runtime to force the legacy kernel for the short term on affected hosts; that reduced error-rate by ~65% in our internal replay.
- We should enable per-customer circuit-break thresholds for Bright Retail while we validate the patch cluster-wide. I propose: 4xx/5xx > 3% sustained for 5m triggers routing to compact variant + 10% credit for impacted tokens (discretionary).

Actions:
- Sean to coordinate cluster patch rollout (in progress).
- Aditya to prepare a short MAP (mutual action plan) and customer-facing communication with the exact ETA for full rollback/patch.
- Karthik please confirm Bright Retail agrees to temporary routing to the compact variant and the proposed credit/comp package.

Marissa
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Lucy Chang <lucy@brightretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bright Retail SRE <sre@brightretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lumen4b: intermittent 504s — temporary fallbacks, throttles, and next steps

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the quick action. Two asks from our side: 
1) ETA: can you give a target time for when we can expect stable service to return to <1% errors? Our promo campaign runs through the weekend and this spike is already affecting cart conversions.
2) Credits: we will request a retroactive service credit for impacted tokens. Please include the proposed credit language in the MAP you mentioned.

We are okay routing select calls to the compact variant for the next 24 hours if the latency profile matches our SLA. Sean: looped you to adjust routing on our end if needed.

—
Lucy Chang
Head of Platform Engineering, Bright Retail
lucy@brightretail.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lucy Chang <lucy@brightretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 14:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Lumen4b: intermittent 504s — temporary fallbacks, throttles, and next steps

Lucy —

Quick recovery update: the hot-patch rollout completed across the affected pools at 13:18 PDT. Error-rate for Bright Retail traffic is now ~0.7% (measured over a 15m window) and tail latency has returned to baseline. We left the compact fallback active for safety for the next 6 hours; we will toggle it off after we verify a full hour at <1% errors.

MAP highlights (short):
- Immediate: Compact fallback active (done) + client-side timeout recommended (requested).
- 0–6h: Continue throttles & tracing; monitor error-rate; credit calculation in progress.
- 24–72h: Postmortem and mitigation plan delivered (postmortem draft link below). Includes long-term kernel fix, rollout calendar, and automated per-customer circuit-break thresholds.

We’ll share the credit calculation once we finish token-level attribution for the impacted window — expect that by EOD tomorrow. Attached is the initial postmortem draft and metrics slice. We will schedule a 30-min sync with Bright Retail stakeholders tomorrow at 10:00 PDT to walk through details and the remediation timeline.

Attachments: [lumen4b-postmortem-draft.md], [lumen4b-throttle-metrics-100K.csv]

Link to draft: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-lumen4b-incident
JIRA: JIRA-INC-8891

Appreciate your patience and flagging this quickly — we’ll follow up with the full RCA and proposed credits.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference
